Where it began

Brian Bennett was born in Harare on 10 November 2003, one of twins. He and his brother David, who also became a professional cricketer, went to Peterhouse Boys' School in Marondera, a school that had already sent Gary Ballance and Ryan Burl into the game. Peterhouse often took teams to a cricket festival at Kingswood College in South Africa, and after leaving school the twins spent a bridging year there, sharpening their cricket.

Both brothers played at the 2022 Under-19 World Cup, where Brian was vice-captain and Zimbabwe's leading scorer with 273 runs, including three fifties.

The player

His first-class career began in unusual fashion. In December 2022 he was brought into a Logan Cup match for Mountaineers as a substitute partway through, and walked out to bat at number five in the second innings. Fourteen months later he hit an unbeaten 264 against Mashonaland Eagles, scoring at a run a ball, and people across the game began to take note.

His Test debut came against Ireland on 25 July 2024. In only his second Test, against Afghanistan at Bulawayo that December, he made an unbeaten 110 from 124 balls as Zimbabwe piled up 586, their biggest Test total, and then took 5 for 95 in the same match. He was 21, and only Hamilton Masakadza had made a Test hundred for Zimbabwe at a younger age. By November 2026 he had played 12 Tests, scoring 568 runs at 31.56 with two hundreds, three fifties and a best of 139, and had held 19 catches.

What made him special

He liked to get on with it. His big innings came at a lively pace, from that Logan Cup 264 to 169 from 163 balls in an ODI win over Ireland in February 2025. At the 2026 T20 World Cup he made an unbeaten 64 as Zimbabwe beat Australia by 23 runs, a famous day for his country, and followed it with 97 not out against India.

His bowling was more of a useful extra than a main weapon, with six Test wickets at 55.83. Then again, five of those came in a single innings, which is a nice way to make the ones you take count.

Away from the middle

In 2024 he was part of the Zimbabwe Emerging side that won the cricket gold medal at the African Games, beating Namibia in the final. His T20 international debut came against Ireland in December 2023, his Test debut the following July and his ODI debut against Pakistan in November 2024, so inside a year he had played all three formats for his country.

And finally

Few cricketers can say their first-class career began halfway through a match. Bennett did not even have to sit through the first innings. He was simply sent in at five and left to work out the rest. He seemed to manage.
